questions.q: What does this lesson recommend structuring the presentation to leadership around?
options: A technical tour of dbt, Snowflake, and GitHub Actions, tool by tool
Leadership's own original complaint from Lesson 1, answered point by point in their own language
A chronological list of every lesson in this capstone
A comparison of Snowflake pricing tiers
questions.explain: Answering their original five-gap complaint directly is a far stronger structure than a generic tool tour.

questions.q: Why does this lesson call the Lesson 23 incident "the strongest single artifact" for this presentation?
options: Because it is the only lesson that mentions Power BI
Because it's a real mistake a reasonable developer could have made, and the platform caught it before any business user saw a wrong number — concrete proof, not an abstract claim
Because it took the longest to build of any lesson in the course
Because it is the only lesson with a quiz
questions.explain: A real, concrete incident with actual blocked-PR evidence is more convincing than describing tests or governance in the abstract.

questions.q: How does this lesson translate "dbt build stops on a failed test" into business language?
options: "The warehouse runs out of compute credits"
"A mistake gets caught before it reaches a dashboard, not after"
"Snowflake automatically deletes bad data"
"Power BI refreshes twice as fast"
questions.explain: The translation restates the technical control in terms of the outcome it guarantees for the business, not the mechanism itself.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say "nothing broke silently" is a stronger pitch than a list of tools used?
options: Because leadership specifically asked for a list of tools in Lesson 1
Because leadership asked for trust in the numbers, not technology for its own sake — the outcome, proven by a real incident, is what actually answers their original ask
Because tools are confidential and cannot be mentioned to leadership
Because a feature list is always technically inaccurate
questions.explain: Leadership's original complaint (Lesson 1) was about trust and visibility, not about which specific tools were used — the outcome is what matters to them.

questions.q: In the lesson's translation table, what does the generated lineage graph get translated to for a non-technical audience?
options: "The warehouse bill is now lower"
"Anyone can see what a number depends on, without asking a developer"
"Power BI reports now load instantly"
"Snowflake automatically writes the dbt models"
questions.explain: The lineage graph's real business value is visibility into dependencies without needing a developer to explain it each time.
